title: Risalat al-anwar fima yumnah sahib al-khalwa min al-asrar (Treatise of Lights: on the secrets granted to one who undertakes retreat)
author: Muhyi al-Din Ibn 'Arabi (d. 638/1240)
edition_cited: Arabic text, excerpt from the OCR of Majmu'at Rasa'il Ibn 'Arabi, vol. 1 (Beirut: Dar al-Mahajja al-Bayda', 2000), archive.org Majmua_Rasail_ibn_Arabi
locator_hints: Line numbers refer to the saved excerpt (subtract nothing: header is 3 lines)

~l. 440-490: conditions before entering retreat: mastering the imagination, diet and balanced temperament ('if dryness is excessive it leads to imaginings'), telling angelic from satanic arrivals by their after-effect; the creed to hold on entering: 'laysa ka-mithlihi shay''; whatever form appears and says 'I am God', say 'subhan Allah'

~l. 540-560: the eye test: when you see the form of a person or an act, 'close your eyes; if the unveiling remains it is in your imagination; if it vanishes, the perception was attached to the place where you saw it'
~l. 550-570: from sensory unveiling to imaginal unveiling; the drinks offered (water, milk, honey; avoid wine)

~l. 660-700: the repeated formula 'fa-in lam taqif ma'a hadha rufi'a laka...' (if you do not stop with this, there is raised for you...): the flashes (lawa'ih), then 'nur mutatayir al-sharar' (a light scattering sparks) from which you seek cover: 'do not fear, keep to the dhikr'; then the light of the ascendants (tawali')
~l. 860: 'a light in which you see none but yourself'
Throughout: the instruction not to halt at any stage and to keep to dhikr
summary: A short letter of practical guidance for retreat. Ibn 'Arabi sets preconditions (discipline before seclusion, control of imagination, moderate diet because excess dryness breeds phantasms, a shaykh if possible), gives a rule for telling angelic from satanic visitations by the state they leave behind, and fixes the attitude to hold: God is like nothing, so whatever form appears claiming divinity is to be dismissed and the dhikr continued. He then lists in order what is 'raised' before the practitioner if he does not stop at each stage: first the sensory world seen through walls and darkness, with a test (close your eyes: if the vision stays it is in imagination, if it goes it was located perception), then imaginal forms and cups, then flashes, a light that throws off sparks and frightens, a light of ascendant stars, and many further unveilings. The repeated counsel is: do not stop with it, do not fear, keep invoking.
why_relevant: States an explicit operational test for imaginal versus located perception with eyes closed, names lights among the phenomena of retreat, and gives the 'do not stop' counsel; seed lead confirmed.
